question: Does exact characteristic luminance plus the zero-luminance chroma of fixed AO6 form a safer and preferred factorized look on a development-only camera population?

operator.luminance: unchanged CB11 epsilon-anchored characteristic luminance at strength 0.2
operator.chroma: C_ao6 = AO6 - dot(AO6, Rec.709 weights); output = Y_cb11 + alpha*C_ao6
operator.scale: one maximum analytical alpha in [0,1] preserving cube and source-relative epsilon boundaries
operator.forbidden: fit, learned selector, per-image strength, hard clipping, Lab compression, spatial mask or post-score rescue

stop_rules: Any automatic failure closes the exact factorization before visual preference and without rescue.
Preference failure closes the exact factorization without strength, population, round or gate changes.
Pass opens only a wholly new source confirmation; this consumed development population cannot promote a product or stock claim.
claim_ceiling: Development-only explicit factorization evidence on previously consumed CC0 display proxies; not fresh confirmation, stock response, calibration, population preference or product promotion.
